about.title: Colma Workplace Injury Claims
about.longDescription: Colma is a small San Mateo County city, but its workforce spans cemetery grounds crews, landscaping operations, retail along El Camino Real, and businesses tucked near Junipero Serra Boulevard. Workplace injuries in this kind of setting often involve heavy equipment, uneven terrain, delivery vehicles, or contractors moving through shared job sites. In most cases, California law channels an injured worker's claim through workers' compensation, regardless of who caused the accident. But when a subcontractor, equipment manufacturer, property owner, or another driver on the road contributed to the harm, a separate third-party injury claim may also be available. Sorting out which path applies, and whether both apply, takes a careful look at how the injury happened. LawProactive doesn't practice law or handle claims directly. We simply connect injured workers in Colma with an independent, contingency-fee attorney who can review the facts and explain the options at no upfront cost.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney About a Colma Workplace Injury

items.title: Workers' Comp Isn't Always the Full Picture
items.desc: California generally treats workers' compensation as the exclusive remedy against an employer, but a negligent third party like a subcontractor or equipment maker can still be held separately liable.

items.title: Reporting Deadlines Matter
items.desc: Workplace injuries generally need to be reported to an employer within 30 days, and missing that window can complicate a claim, so timing matters from day one.

items.title: Retaliation Is Against the Law
items.desc: An employer cannot legally punish a worker for reporting an injury or pursuing a claim, and an attorney can help address concerns about workplace pressure.

items.question: I was hurt at a job site near Junipero Serra Boulevard. Do I file workers' comp or a lawsuit?
items.answer: In most cases, workers' compensation is the first and exclusive path against your employer, regardless of fault. If a third party, such as a subcontractor, driver, or equipment manufacturer, contributed to the accident, a separate injury claim may also be possible. An attorney can review the specifics of your situation to identify which options apply.

items.question: How long do I have to report a workplace injury in Colma?
items.answer: California generally requires workers to report an injury to their employer within 30 days. Waiting longer can make it harder to establish the claim, so it's worth reporting as soon as reasonably possible after the incident.

items.question: What if my employer retaliates after I report an injury?
items.answer: Retaliation for reporting a workplace injury is illegal under California law. If you're facing pressure, demotion, or termination connected to a claim, an attorney can advise you on your rights and next steps.
